summary: Step 4 replaces iteration 1's funnel (rare AND protein-altering AND biallelic AND PASS — a gene is in or out) with a multiplier: every piece of evidence becomes a likelihood ratio (a multiplier on how much more or less likely a gene is to be causal), nothing is a hard cutoff, and every one of the 11,465 protein-coding genes with a scorable pair gets a ranked answer. It scored 51,920 biallelic hypotheses — 35,120 compound (two different damaged alleles), 14,130 homozygous (one allele on both copies), 2,670 single (one damaged allele, no partner — the shape a hard filter deletes outright) — combining a genotype half (consequence severity, population frequency, AlphaMissense/SpliceAI/ClinVar evidence, non-PASS down-weighting) with a phenotype half (a likelihood ratio read directly off step 1's own measured recall curve, so an uncurated gene gets a ratio below 1, never zero). BUB1B leads genome-wide at ratio 341,019, compound, with ADAMTS1 runner-up at 201,029 (only 1.70x behind, and phased in cis — both alleles on the same copy, so it is not actually a compound-heterozygote hypothesis). Of six pre-registered claims, three were supported and three refuted, and the refutations are described as the more useful half of the result.
why: Steps 1–3 each independently measured the cost of iteration 1's cut-based funnel: symptom-only recall tops out at 0.335, three-quarters of protein-coding genes carry no phenotype curation at all, and the read-derived route's discrimination power measured at zero (targets and decoys were statistically indistinguishable before any filter, in step 2's own H020 result). A cut applied early on any one of those axes permanently deletes evidence nobody can retrieve downstream — an early filter cannot be un-filtered by a later step. Multiplying instead of cutting is the only way to let a true answer survive being uncurated, being frequency-borderline, or lacking a caller-flagged partner allele, while still producing one ranked answer across the entire coding genome rather than only across step 1's 404-gene enrichment set.
verdict: H030 (the genome-wide top pair sits in a step-1 target gene) is supported: BUB1B, tier core. H031 (the runner-up is ≥10x behind) is refuted — ADAMTS1 is only 1.70x behind, though it is phased cis and therefore not a valid compound-het hypothesis at all. H032 (no uncurated gene reaches the top 20) is refuted: ADAMTS1 has no phenotype curation and reached rank 2, entering through the phenotype lane's unranked bucket (not the network-proximity lane built for exactly this case, which fired for no top-25 gene) and overcoming its 0.379x penalty on genotype evidence alone. H033 (<1 in 1,000 permuted symptom sets reach the leader) is refuted: 55 of 1,000 do, almost entirely because HLA-DRB1's extreme polymorphism gets promoted by unrelated term permutations — the null is measuring HLA hyperpolymorphism as much as phenotype specificity. H034 (targets separate from matched decoys) is supported at AUC 0.706 [0.655, 0.751], which is the step's strongest result because step 2 had already shown the same two gene sets indistinguishable before any scoring (10/396 each). H035 (the lead pair's P(trans), the probability the two alleles sit on opposite copies, is undetermined) is supported: only 5 of 50 leading alleles even appear in the population reference database (gnomAD v2), so P(trans) cannot be computed for any of the top 25 pairs, not just the leader.

inherits.what: The phenotype lane's likelihood ratio is read directly off step 1's measured recall-at-rank curve, not an invented conversion — step 4 could not exist without that curve being a measured quantity rather than an assumption. Step 2's decoy set (H020: unfiltered targets and decoys indistinguishable) is what makes H034's AUC meaningful as attributable to the scoring rather than the gene list. Step 3's dosage finding (both lead alleles at one copy each) and its measured per-origin allele error rates feed the genotype-half evidence for the lead pair.

hands_to.what: Step 5's knowledge engine takes the top-20 genome-wide gene list to build its literature/mechanism case. Step 6's fusion takes both leads (BUB1B and ADAMTS1, with the reason ADAMTS1 is not really a compound-het hypothesis attached to its row rather than filtered out), the measured AUC 0.706 separation, the measured non-specificity (p=0.056, with the HLA explanation), and the fact that P(trans) is undetermined for every leading pair — placing the lead pair in the failure category 'unphaseable: both alleles real, both single-copy, no fragment spanning them, no parental DNA' that step 6 has to reason through explicitly rather than assume away.

figures.name: leaders.png
figures.reads: Log-scale horizontal bars of the top 20 genome-wide hypotheses by combined likelihood ratio, colour-coded: green = step-1 symptom-nominated target gene, purple = a gene with no phenotype curation, blue = curated but not nominated, red = a matched decoy.
figures.means: BUB1B leads at 341,019; no red (decoy) bar appears among the top 20, which is itself evidence for H034's separation — the decoys, scored by the identical pipeline, do not compete with real candidates. The ratio orders hypotheses; it is explicitly not a calibrated probability that a gene is causal.

figures.name: decomposition.png
figures.reads: Log10-scale bars, one per scoring lane (phenotype rank, left-allele consequence, left-allele frequency, right-allele AlphaMissense, right-allele frequency, etc.), for BUB1B's leading hypothesis, summing to its total log-ratio; a lane at zero was consulted but damped because it shares a correlation group with a stronger lane.
figures.means: Shows the mechanism in full: BUB1B's ratio is built from a truncating/NMD-competent allele (×350) paired with an AlphaMissense likely_pathogenic missense allele (×4.33), both absent from gnomAD (×2.08 each), plus the phenotype rank-6-of-5,259 lane (×52.08) — reproducing, without being told it, the null-plus-hypomorph genetic model described in Hanks 2004 (PMID 15475955) for this disease class.

figures.name: groups.png
figures.reads: Bars per gene class (targets vs. matched decoys) showing the median and 90th-percentile likelihood ratio of each class, with a dotted line at ratio = 1.
figures.means: Direct visual evidence for H034: target genes sit well above decoys and above the ratio-1 line, even though step 2 measured the same two gene sets as statistically indistinguishable before any scoring — so the separation shown here is produced entirely by the likelihood-ratio scoring, not by which genes happened to be on the list.

figures.name: permutation-null.png
figures.reads: Histogram of the top likelihood ratio reached by 1,000 random seven-term symptom sets (each matched to the child's own term-depth profile), with a dashed line marking the observed leader's ratio.
figures.means: Evidence for H033's refutation: 55 of 1,000 random draws reach or exceed the observed leader (p=0.056, not <0.001), but only four genes in the entire callset can ever exceed that value under any term set, and almost every exceeding draw is HLA-DRB1 being promoted — meaning the apparent non-specificity is mostly an artefact of HLA hyperpolymorphism, not evidence the symptom set is uninformative.

figures.name: genotype-only.png
figures.reads: Paired bars per top gene: green = the combined ranking as reported, blue = the same hypothesis re-scored with the phenotype lane fixed at 1 (no symptom contribution) for every gene.
figures.means: The ablation control for H030: the combined ranking's leader is not the leader when phenotype is removed — on DNA alone, BUB1B falls to joint third behind ADAMTS1 and HLA-DRB1. This is the honest reading of H030's support: the claim holds for the two routes (symptoms + DNA) together, not for a DNA-only genome-wide scan.

figures.name: phenotype-bins.png
figures.reads: Bars per rank band (e.g. top-50, 51–300, uncurated) showing the likelihood ratio for that band, derived as the fraction of the 3,240-disease benchmark's causal genes landing in that band divided by the fraction of all genes the band contains; dotted line at ratio = 1.
figures.means: Shows the step's core methodological move: the phenotype-to-likelihood conversion is measured from step 1's own held-out benchmark rather than invented, and the uncurated bucket sits below 1 but never at 0 — which is exactly what lets an uncurated gene like ADAMTS1 still climb the genome-wide ranking on genotype evidence alone.

figures.name: lane-coverage.png
figures.reads: Bars showing how many allele slots each evidence lane (AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, ClinVar, consequence class alone, or no lane at all) actually won across the run, per consequence class.
figures.means: AlphaMissense covers 10,601 alleles and wins 22.2% of all allele slots, the single largest lane, while CADD and LOFTEE contribute nothing because Ensembl's REST endpoint does not serve either plugin — recorded as an absence rather than worked around, which caps how much fine-grained missense/splice evidence the ranking can actually draw on for most alleles.

figures.name: shapes.png
figures.reads: One bar per biallelic hypothesis shape (compound, homozygous, single), labelled with the gene count behind each.
figures.means: 35,120 compound, 14,130 homozygous, 2,670 single hypotheses were all scored — including the 'single' shape (one damaged allele, no partner) that a hard filter would delete outright, kept here at the square root of its evidence because a missing partner may reflect a call the pipeline never made rather than a genuinely intact second copy.

figures.name: index.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet of all eight figures (leaders, decomposition, groups, permutation-null, genotype-only, phenotype-bins, lane-coverage, shapes) with hover tooltips for exact values.
figures.means: Same evidence as the eight static figures, in a form a reader can inspect value-by-value rather than reading off a static image.
